selection: All16 OpenStack Glance training candidates across all statuses; no null-category candidates exist in this repository.
interpretation: Training-only matched old-contract/delivery review: seven missing-context, eight security-boundary and one residual paired-negative deferral. Exact owner versus visibility checks support two API-order defects, but v2 after still queues builtin id. Six Swift add/get diagnostics have exact client-visible error consumers; three deletion rows instead have absorbing raw-URI-log wrappers, two ACL rows normally lack credentials and three parser rows need malformed-private-input/log audience. Fourteen Swift candidates/backports remain one family; v2 advisory explicitly describes incomplete v1 fix without establishing issue independence. Preserve every discovery event, previous authored batch, source byte/split and45 protected inputs. All application, auth/policy, DB/SQL, Swift/storage, HTTP/WSGI/parser, dependency programs, requests and upstream tests remain inert; deductions are not reproduced failures.

reviews.mechanism: v1 backend destruction or queueing occurs before registry owner authorization.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Preserve existing resource-authorization, credential-diagnostic-disclosure or validation-secret-logging leaf. Distinguish visibility/generic policy from owner mutation, private backend credentials from user-known URI data, client-visible errors from operational logs, and default token/credential-free ACL locations from single-tenant service locations. No consequence-only relabelling or independent-issue count follows.
reviews.contract_reason: Old SQL image_get checks visibility, which includes public or shared images. check_mutate_authorization separately restricts mutations to admin or matching owner; image_update/image_destroy invoke it. The old mutating decorator rejects read_only contexts but is not an ownership check. Generic action policy uses an empty resource target and permissive defaults; passing it and reading a public non-protected image does not authorize deletion. Old backend effect precedes the owner check, so a nonowner with ordinary writable request context and action-policy admission can destroy image data before the later registry/DB rejection. This is an existing cross-tenant authorization duty, not a newly restrictive policy. Exact old BaseController forwards request context to registry metadata lookup; registry update/delete preserve that context and delegate to SQL owner checks. The selected function itself misorders these operations.
reviews.context_reason: Need mutating/read-only wrapper, generic policy, BaseController metadata visibility, registry context/client forwarding, registry mutation endpoints, SQL owner checks and actual store effect. The common before-only numerical budget and ordinary runtime/API/tool-knowledge policy remain unfrozen. Matched helpers/callers, globals, policy/configuration, after, tests, advisories and answers are adjudication-only, never selectively added to detection input.
reviews.security_reason: A nonadmin authenticated caller, non-read-only context, admitted delete action and readable public/shared victim image with protected false and nonempty location supply the source-supported route. Default immediate deletion is sufficient: the service store deletes by URI, not by caller ownership. Backend/service credentials and OS/store success matter. A private unreadable or protected image is not the witness, and no identity-header forgery, anonymous access or actual deployment is assumed.
reviews.negative_reason: After completes both registry mutations before invoking backend delete/queue. A registry Forbidden/NotFound now exits before the witnessed unauthorized backend effect. This is a bounded authorization-order negative, not transaction rollback, guaranteed authorized cleanup, retry safety, all backend failures or all credential/log confidentiality.
reviews.subset_reason: The local historical repair and conditional trust-boundary path are supported, but essential old producer/caller/authorization/backend contracts are unavailable in the proposed before-only function.
reviews.dependence_reason: Preserve fix-family:c2bbe07a761cb2da3788 and exact/AST/span/history relationships. Fourteen Swift rows across three historical commits are one CVE-linked mechanical family, not14 independent disclosures. The v1 and v2 authorization rows retain distinct families; the retained v2 advisory explicitly calls it an incomplete-fix follow-up to v1, so do not infer independence or merge issue identities merely from different API versions/CVEs. All16 rows/three mechanical families are review units, not adjudicated issues.
